framework.notes: references/django.md was loaded in addition to references/python.md and references/patterns.md. Its source cues (request.GET/POST/body, route parameters, serializer validated_data) map onto the observed code: function views read request.GET/POST and CBV handler methods (APIBase(View) subclasses such as MVT.get(self, request, nodeid, zoom, x, y)) receive URL route parameters directly. Its sink cues (cursor.execute, .raw) are half-observed: cursor.execute is the dominant channel, but .raw()/RawSQL()/.extra()/from_statement do not exist in project code (see sinkFamilies.absentChannels) so no rules were fabricated for them. request.user / request.method / request.LANGUAGE_CODE reads were observed but are framework-computed identity/state rather than raw attacker text and are not emitted as source families.

inputBoundaryInventory.summary: Attackers face (1) the Django HTTP surface: request.GET (181 reads in arches/app), request.POST (91), request.body JSON payloads (29), request.FILES (12), request.META (9) and URL route parameters (uuid route params such as conceptid/nodeid plus non-uuid zoom/x/y path segments); function views (concept.py, search.py, api.py, etl_manager.py, ...) and APIBase(View)/View subclass handler methods (get/post) are the dispatch boundary registered in arches/urls.py; (2) the CLI surface of 40+ django management commands whose add_argument/options values (including DB role names and table names) reach string-built SQL in setup_db.py, export.py and packages.py; (3) the filesystem: packages.py load_sql()/load_resource_views() read entire .sql files from operator-supplied package directories and execute them verbatim; ETL uploads are staged under uploadedfiles/<loadid>; (4) the Postgres DB itself: concept values, tile primary keys and ORM lookups are re-interpolated into SQL (intermediate propagation, not external input); (5) settings/environment: operator-level trust (DATABASES credentials, os.environ in settings_docker.py). The dominant SQL execution channel is django.db connection.cursor() + cursor.execute(); 74 .execute( sites exist in arches/ overall, of which the ETL import modules, the MVT/buffer map endpoints and the etl_manager views are fully parameterized, while a handful of concept/RDM paths interpolate request-derived values into the SQL text.

extraction.executionPlan: codeql query run (sequential, one at a time) + codeql bqrs decode --format=csv; NOT database analyze / SARIF. Execution is deferred to the next round per the task contract (generation only).
extraction.metadataForm: plain multi-column select queries carrying @name/@description/@id/@tags only; intentionally no @kind problem (wrong shape for multi-column candidate tables) and no @kind table (not assumed to exist).
columnContract: node (location-backed AST node; decodes as file:line:col)
arg_index (0-based positional argument index, -1 when not applicable)
match_kind ('api' = resolved real API call via API graphs, 'ast' = syntax-level match)

matchKindSemantics.api: call resolved through semmle.python.ApiGraphs; in this project NO sink or source row is expected to resolve at API level: all SQL execution flows through local cursor variables (cursor = connection.cursor() / self.dbcursor / schema_editor parameters) that API graphs cannot bind to django.db or psycopg2 members, and the Django request object is a framework-injected value, not a module member. The column is kept for cross-project contract consistency.
matchKindSemantics.ast: pure AST shape match (attribute/name text, syntactic receiver, request/field/settings/options name conventions). All execute/callproc matches are receiver-name-agnostic (any <obj>.execute(...) / <obj>.callproc(...) call matches), which tolerates cursor aliasing (cursor, dbcursor, schema_editor) but cannot prove the receiver is a database cursor - name-collision noise is possible and is left to the labeling step.

exclusions: paths containing /tests/ or /fixtures/ (the database snapshot covers tests/, docker/ and repo-root scripts; tests are excluded from candidates per the workflow noise rules)
/arches-db/ and /arches-safe-db/ (CodeQL database directories nested inside the source tree)
extraction.expectedVolume: roughly 1500-2500 source rows (request attribute reads ~320, request .get() reads ~280, handler parameters ~400, cli add_argument/options ~350, settings config reads ~400, file open/read ~100, internal_transfer call args ~200, env/sys.argv sparse) and roughly 200-400 sink rows (74 execute sites + bound-param companion rows + construction nodes inside ~35 SQL wrapper functions + wrapper function rows). This is in line with prior projects in this series (maltrail 617/52, pgadmin4 2150/61).

uncoveredCases: Positional-argument scan cap: the http_body family (index of the request.body argument) and the internal_transfer family (index of a transferred positional argument) enumerate argument positions 0-9 (i is bound by range membership before the indexed Call.getPositionalArg(i) lookup, because the index parameter of getPositionalArg is a checked/total-function input in QL); calls with more than 10 positional arguments would not be scanned. No such call exists on the SQL-relevant paths in this snapshot.

Binding-analysis hardening (verified by codeql query compile): excludedPath(string path) carries a bindingset[path] annotation because path only appears in checked positions (receiver of replaceAll/matches) inside the predicate; without the annotation the compiler reports 'path is not bound to a value'. Both queries compile clean (exit 0, no warnings) against codeql 2.25.1 + codeql/python-all resolved from the local pack cache via iris/qlpack.yml.

Keyword-argument hand-off: get_child_collections_hierarchically passes query=query / offset= / limit= as KEYWORD arguments to get_child_edges (arches/app/models/concept.py:464-467); internal_transfer rows cover positional arguments only, so the request-derived query keyword binding is not captured as a call-argument row. Mitigation: the query parameter itself is captured by the handler-param family (paged_dropdown's request.GET.get) and the construction+execute sites in get_child_edges are captured by the sink query.

packages.py load_sql/load_resource_views (arches/management/commands/packages.py:604-629): SQL text is read from a whole file into a variable (sql = f.read()) and executed - no string-construction expression exists, so only the execute row and the open()/read() source rows represent this path; the file->variable->execute data flow is not traced at extraction time.

SQL text variables: all 'execute(sql)' sites where sql is a plain local variable (concept.py view/model, index_database, datatypes, tasks, system_metadata) are captured as execute rows; the variable assignment chain (which construction expression fed sql) is only captured when the construction sits inside the same executing function - cross-function construction is not traced.

Dynamic receiver identity: <obj>.execute(...) matching is syntactic; whether the receiver is a django.db cursor, a psycopg2 cursor or an unrelated object with an execute method is not resolved. In this snapshot every .execute( site found by grep is a database cursor, but the query tolerates collisions by design.

Celery task boundary: tasks.load_single_csv.apply_async((self.userid, self.loadid, graphid, ...)) (arches/app/etl_modules/import_single_csv.py:163-166) - task argument tuples are not modeled as a source family; the ETL-side SQL is parameterized anyway.

Django ORM model-manager calls (models.X.objects.filter(...)) and route->view dispatch (urls.py -> as_view()) are framework-internal and not extracted; ORM raw channels are absent (see sinkFamilies.channelInventory.absentChannels).

request.user / request.method / request.LANGUAGE_CODE / request.GET.copy() are framework-computed or container state; request.data / request.query_params / request.headers / request.COOKIES (DRF shapes) are NOT observed in this project and are not emitted.

The concept() view's depth_limit request input is dead (overwritten at arches/app/views/concept.py:115); its get_child_concepts/depth_limit SQL slot is therefore constant on the reachable path - recorded here rather than as a candidate.
